rounds.hypothesis: Taken from diagnose: the legacy `struct termio` ioctl family (TCGETA 0x5405, TCSETA 0x5406, TCSETAW 0x5407, TCSETAF 0x5408) is absent from the whole tree, so 0x5405 falls off the end of every tty dispatch and hits a default arm that returns ENOTTY before any argument is touched. The two failing assertions want EFAULT from the copy-out/copy-in of a bad user pointer, so the errno is being decided by cmd recognition rather than pointer validity. Defining the userspace type plus four arms in the shared `Tty::ioctl` -- and forwarding them from the pty master to its slave -- should make the fault actually be reached, without touching any default ENOTTY arm.
rounds.change: Four files, +127/-6 (one of which is the pool file). (a) kernel/src/device/tty/termio.rs: added `CTermio`, an 18-byte `#[padding_struct] #[repr(C)]` Pod (four u16 flag words, u8 c_line, [u8; 8] c_cc) with `const_assert!(size_of::<CTermio>() == 18)`; `From<&CTermios> for CTermio` narrows each flag word to u16, copies c_line, and copies the first 8 of the 19 control chars, starting from `FromZeros::new_zeroed()` so the trailing pad byte cannot leak kernel data; `CTermio::apply_to(&CTermios) -> CTermios` is the reverse, replacing only the low 16 bits of each flag word and the first 8 control chars via a `merge_low_bits` helper that round-trips through `u32` with Pod `as_bytes`/`from_bytes` so undefined bits are preserved rather than truncated. (b) ioctl_defs.rs: four `ioc!` aliases in the legacy form, next to the TCGETS block. (c) tty/mod.rs: four arms mirroring the existing GetTermios/SetTermios/SetTermiosWait/SetTermiosFlush arms, the setters going through `on_termios_change` + `set_termios` and SetTermioFlush additionally doing `drain_input()` + `pollee.invalidate()`. (d) pty/master.rs: added the four aliases to the forwarding whitelist. No default arm changed.
rounds.outcome: green on the first round. `PATH=<osdk_bin> VNC_PORT=2228 CARGO_OSDK=<...> make run_kernel AUTO_TEST=conformance CONFORMANCE_TEST_SELECTOR=ioctl01 RELEASE=1 NETDEV=user` printed `All conformance tests passed.` with `ioctl01: pass (0.001s)` at qemu.log:43 -- a `pass` verdict means all 9 assertions TPASS, so the 2 TCGETA-pointer cases now return EFAULT while the 4 ENOTTY/EBADF traps still hold. `make check` (clippy + rustfmt) exit 0, no warnings.

layer: The shared TTY ioctl layer -- `Tty::ioctl` in kernel/src/device/tty/mod.rs plus the type definitions in tty/termio.rs and tty/ioctl_defs.rs -- exactly the `owning_layer` diagnose named, and the Asterinas counterpart of Linux's `tty_mode_ioctl`. The pty master's whitelist in device/pty/master.rs is extended in the same change, but only to forward: it holds no handling logic, so the four commands resolve in the one generic `Tty<D>` that all four drivers instantiate. Handling them in `PtyMaster` instead would have turned ioctl01 green while leaving serial, hvc and vt returning ENOTTY for TCGETA.
generalizes:
The fix is the general rule, not the tested path. It adds the whole legacy family (TCGETA/TCSETA/TCSETAW/TCSETAF) at the layer every TTY shares, so all four `TtyDriver` implementations named in `other_callers` gain it at once -- PtySlave, SerialDriver (/dev/ttyS0 and the console), HvcDriver (/dev/hvc0) and VtDriver -- even though ioctl01 only ever touches a pty master. Nothing branches on the flag, size, or errno the test happens to use: ioctl01 exercises only TCGETA, and only its failure mode, yet TCGETA's success path and all three setters are implemented too, which is why the extra verification below was worth running.

The conversions are correct for inputs the test never supplies, and this was pinned against the host rather than assumed. A host probe (/tmp/tcseta/p.c) sets EXTPROC (0x10000, expressible only in the high half of c_lflag) and c_cc[17] (beyond the legacy NCC=8), then does a TCGETA/TCSETA round-trip: Linux preserves both. `apply_to` preserves both for the same reason -- it merges only the low 16 bits and only c_cc[..8], leaving the rest of the kernel's `CTermios2` untouched -- so a legacy-termio caller cannot silently clobber modern state, and `merge_low_bits` goes through raw bytes rather than `from_bits_truncate` specifically so undefined flag bits survive, matching what the existing TCSETS path already does with its byte-copy read. The 18-byte size is the userspace ABI (verified against `sizeof(struct termio)` on the host, and against `offsetof(c_cc) == 9`) and is now held by a `const_assert!`, because the legacy ioctl encoding carries no size field and so nothing else in the dispatch machinery would catch a drift there -- and no ioctl01 case performs a *successful* TCGETA, so the test alone would not have caught it either.

The four negative traps diagnose flagged are all preserved and measured green in the same run: a regular-file fd still returns ENOTTY through `InodeHandle::ioctl` (tcases 5, 6, untouched -- nothing outside the tty tree was modified), cmd 9999999 still returns ENOTTY (tcase 4, the default arms are unchanged), and fd -1 still returns EBADF ahead of cmd decoding (tcases 0, 1, resolved in `sys_ioctl`). EFAULT arrives the required way, from the `cmd.write`/`cmd.read` copy rather than an early pointer check, so it is a real fault report and not a second special case.

Regression evidence beyond the target: the gvisor `pty_test` binary -- the tree's densest termios coverage, packaged in CI with 35 of its cases blocked -- ran its enabled set and the whole default gvisor suite came back 81/81 test cases passed, including TermiosFault, Termios2, DefaultTermios, TermiosAffectsReplica, MasterTermiosUnchangable, TermiosICRNL/ONLCR and TCSETSFTermiosICRNL/ONLCR, i.e. exactly the setter and copy-fault paths adjacent to the new arms. Both boots also ran their console on hvc0 through this same `Tty::ioctl`, so the shared layer is exercised for a non-pty driver by the act of booting.
fix_summary:
Implement the legacy System V `struct termio` mode ioctls in the shared TTY layer, so TCGETA/TCSETA/TCSETAW/TCSETAF work wherever TCGETS/TCSETS/TCSETSW/TCSETSF do, and a bad argument pointer to them reports EFAULT instead of being masked by ENOTTY for an unrecognised command.

The abstraction chosen is a *pure boundary type*: `CTermio` exists only as a userspace representation and has no presence in kernel state. Asterinas already keeps one internal `CTermios2` in the line discipline, which is the same design Linux uses with its single `struct ktermios`, so the legacy/modern split needs to exist only at the copy-in/copy-out edge. That made a `From<&CTermios> for CTermio` plus a `CTermio::apply_to(&CTermios) -> CTermios` pair the whole fix; no second internal representation, no change to `LineDiscipline`, and the four new dispatch arms end in the same `set_termios`/`drain_input` calls their termios counterparts already use.

Where Asterinas differs from Linux, the local abstraction won. Linux's flag words are plain `tcflag_t`, so its `user_termio_to_kernel_termios` merges them with open-coded masking; Asterinas wraps three of the four in `bitflags` types and the fourth (`CCtrlFlags`) in a newtype, and neither `from_bits_truncate` (lossy for undefined bits) nor bitflags 1.3's `from_bits_unchecked` (unsafe, and the kernel crate is `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`) was acceptable. The `merge_low_bits` helper instead reuses the tree's own `Pod` guarantee -- every one of these types is `#[repr(C)]` over a u32 -- to do the merge on bytes, safely and without discarding bits, with a `const` size assertion so it cannot be applied to a type it does not fit. Padding is likewise handled the Asterinas way: `#[padding_struct]` makes the ABI's single trailing pad byte an explicit field, which is what lets the type derive `Pod` at all (zerocopy's `IntoBytes` rejects implicit padding) and what makes zero-initialising it enough to guarantee the pad byte carries no kernel data to userspace.

The setters deliberately go through `set_termios`, not `set_termios2`: like legacy `struct termios`, `struct termio` encodes line speed in the c_cflag baud bits, and `set_termios` is the existing entry point that recomputes `CTermiosSpeeds` from those bits. `SetTermioWait` carries the same "drain the output buffer" TODO as the existing `SetTermiosWait`, inheriting rather than diverging from that known gap.
